Influenza.description: A viral infection of the respiratory tract that causes sudden fever, body aches and exhaustion. It spreads easily through coughing and sneezing.
precautions: Rest and drink plenty of fluids
Take fever medicine only as advised by a doctor
Cover your mouth while coughing or sneezing
Stay home to avoid spreading the virus

Common Cold.description: A mild viral infection of the nose and throat. Symptoms usually build slowly and clear up within a week to ten days.
precautions: Drink warm fluids and stay hydrated
Get enough rest
Wash your hands frequently
Avoid close contact with people who are unwell

COVID-19.description: An infectious respiratory illness caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus. It can range from mild cold-like symptoms to serious breathing difficulty.
precautions: Isolate yourself and wear a mask around others
Monitor your oxygen level if a device is available
Seek urgent care for breathing difficulty
Follow local testing and vaccination guidance

Malaria.description: A mosquito-borne infection caused by Plasmodium parasites. It typically produces cycles of high fever, chills and sweating.
precautions: Get a blood test for malaria as soon as possible
Use mosquito nets and repellents
Avoid stagnant water near your home
Complete the full course of prescribed medicine

Dengue.description: A viral infection spread by Aedes mosquitoes. High fever, severe headache and body pain are common, and platelet levels may drop.
precautions: Drink fluids to prevent dehydration
Use paracetamol for fever, not aspirin or ibuprofen
Get a platelet count checked if symptoms worsen
Prevent mosquito breeding around your home

Typhoid.description: A bacterial infection spread through contaminated food and water. It causes prolonged fever, stomach pain and weakness.
precautions: Drink only boiled or filtered water
Eat freshly cooked food and wash fruit
Get a blood culture or Widal test if fever persists
Complete the prescribed antibiotic course

Pneumonia.description: An infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs. It can cause phlegm, chest pain and difficulty breathing.
precautions: Seek medical care promptly, especially with breathlessness
Take prescribed antibiotics or antivirals as directed
Rest and drink warm fluids
Avoid smoking and second-hand smoke

Bronchial Asthma.description: A chronic condition in which the airways narrow and swell, causing wheezing, coughing and breathlessness, often triggered by allergens.
precautions: Keep your rescue inhaler with you
Avoid dust, smoke and known triggers
Follow your asthma action plan
Get urgent help if breathing does not improve

Diabetes Mellitus.description: A metabolic condition in which blood sugar stays too high. Early signs include thirst, frequent urination and unexplained weight loss.
precautions: Get a fasting blood sugar or HbA1c test
Limit sugary drinks and refined carbohydrates
Exercise for at least 30 minutes most days
Never ignore a foot wound or persistent thirst

Hypertension.description: Persistently high blood pressure that often has no obvious symptoms but raises the risk of heart, kidney and stroke problems.
precautions: Check your blood pressure regularly
Reduce salt and processed food
Stay physically active and manage stress
Take prescribed medicine without skipping doses

Migraine.description: A neurological condition that causes recurring throbbing headaches, often with nausea and sensitivity to light or sound.
precautions: Rest in a quiet, dark room during an attack
Identify and avoid triggers such as skipped meals or poor sleep
Keep a headache diary
Do not overuse painkillers without medical advice

Gastroenteritis.description: Inflammation of the stomach and intestines, usually caused by a viral or bacterial infection. It leads to diarrhoea, vomiting and cramps.
precautions: Use oral rehydration solution frequently
Eat light, bland food as tolerated
Wash hands after using the toilet
Seek care if there is blood in stool or signs of dehydration

Hepatitis B.description: A viral infection that attacks the liver. It can cause jaundice, dark urine, fatigue and abdominal discomfort.
precautions: Get a hepatitis B blood test and medical review
Avoid alcohol completely
Do not share razors, needles or toothbrushes
Ensure family members are vaccinated

Urinary Tract Infection.description: A bacterial infection of the urinary system. It commonly causes a burning sensation, frequent urination and cloudy urine.
precautions: Drink plenty of water
Do not hold urine for long periods
Take prescribed antibiotics for the full course
Seek care promptly if you develop fever or back pain

Anemia.description: A condition with fewer healthy red blood cells than normal, leading to tiredness, pale skin and breathlessness on exertion.
precautions: Get a complete blood count test
Eat iron-rich foods such as leafy greens and legumes
Take iron supplements only as prescribed
Investigate heavy periods or blood loss with a doctor

Hypothyroidism.description: An underactive thyroid gland slows metabolism, causing tiredness, weight gain, dry skin and feeling cold.
precautions: Ask for a thyroid function test (TSH, T3, T4)
Take thyroid medicine consistently as prescribed
Do not start supplements without medical advice
Get periodic thyroid checks during pregnancy

Osteoarthritis.description: Wear-and-tear of joint cartilage that causes pain, stiffness and swelling, most often in the knees, hips and lower back.
precautions: Maintain a healthy body weight
Do low-impact exercise such as swimming or cycling
Use heat or cold packs for relief
Ask a doctor before taking long-term painkillers

Allergic Rhinitis.description: An allergic reaction affecting the nose and eyes, causing sneezing, a runny nose, itchy eyes and congestion.
precautions: Avoid pollen, dust and pet dander where possible
Keep windows closed during high pollen periods
Ask a doctor about antihistamines
Wash bedding regularly in hot water

Sinusitis.description: Inflammation of the sinuses that causes facial pressure, a blocked nose and headache, often after a cold.
precautions: Use steam inhalation to ease congestion
Stay hydrated
Saline nasal rinses can help
See a doctor if symptoms last more than ten days

Tonsillitis.description: Infection of the tonsils that causes a severe sore throat, painful swallowing and swollen neck glands.
precautions: Drink warm fluids and rest your voice
Gargle with warm salt water
Take antibiotics only if prescribed
Seek care if swallowing or breathing becomes difficult

Chickenpox.description: A highly contagious viral infection that causes an itchy rash with fluid-filled blisters, along with fever and tiredness.
precautions: Avoid scratching to prevent skin infection
Keep nails short and take cool baths
Stay away from pregnant women and newborns
Consult a doctor about antiviral treatment

Tuberculosis.description: A bacterial infection that usually affects the lungs. A persistent cough, night sweats and weight loss are warning signs.
precautions: Get a sputum test and chest X-ray done
Cover your mouth and wear a mask indoors
Take the full six-month course if diagnosed
Ensure close contacts are screened

Kidney Stones.description: Hard mineral deposits in the urinary tract that can cause severe flank pain, blood in urine and nausea.
precautions: Drink plenty of water throughout the day
Reduce excess salt and oxalate-rich foods
Do not ignore severe or worsening flank pain
Get urine and imaging tests if symptoms persist

Peptic Ulcer.description: A painful sore in the lining of the stomach or small intestine. It often causes burning stomach pain and bloating.
precautions: Avoid alcohol, smoking and excess caffeine
Do not take painkillers such as ibuprofen without advice
Eat smaller, regular meals
Get tested for H. pylori infection

Meningitis.description: An inflammation of the membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord. It is a medical emergency that can worsen rapidly.
precautions: Treat this as an emergency and seek hospital care immediately
Do not wait for all symptoms to appear
Avoid close contact with others until assessed
Ask about vaccination for close contacts
